chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, who said:

When you perform ghusl from janābah, then say: O Allah, purify my heart, accept my effort, and make what is with You better for me. O Allah, make me among those who constantly repent, and make me among those who purify themselves.

And when you perform ghusl for Friday, then say: O Allah, purify my heart from every affliction by which my religion is effaced and my deeds are nullified. O Allah, make me among those who constantly repent, and make me among those who purify themselves.

key_terms.التَّوَّابِينَ: those who frequently repent and return to Allah
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: the state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.سَعْيِي: my effort; my striving and deeds
key_terms.قَلْبِي: my heart; the inner self and spiritual center

ai.seo_question: What du'a should be recited during ghusl from janābah and on Friday according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches specific du'as to be recited during ghusl from janābah and the Friday ghusl. It links outward ritual purification with inward purification of the heart, repentance, and the acceptance of one's deeds. The supplication emphasizes that true tahārah includes both bodily cleansing and spiritual reform.
